data.raw_text:
Super Featherweight Champion Flash Elorde wins a controversial 10-round, non-title fight, split decision over Frankie Narvaez (robed), on August 4, 1965, at Madison Square Garden that leads to a post-fight riot.

After a very spirited, and close, bout a ringside poll of 26 sportswriters had 13 scoring it for Narvaez, 9 scoring it for Elorde and 4 scoring it a draw.

The unofficial UPI scorecard had it 4-3-3 for Narvaez, while the unofficial AP scorecard had it a 5-5 draw.

UPI would report:

"Flash Elorde of the Philippines took a split decision Wednesday night over Frankie Narvaez of Puerto Rico in a bout so close that angered Narvaez fans rioted, causing five injuries and five arrests and more than $10,000 damage to MSG. Although he got off to a slow start against the younger Narvaez, Elorde used his 15 years experience to fight his way back. Narvaez dominated the first five rounds, but after that Elorde boxed carefully, counter-punched effectively and finally opened a bad cut beside Narvaez' right eye in the 7th round. Elorde himself had suffered a slight cut beside the right eye in the 5th round but it didn't seem to bother him. Narvaez' cut, however, bled profusely and he repeatedly shook his head trying to clear the blood away. Narvaez tried hard for a knockout in the last two rounds, fearing the doctor might stop the fight, but Elorde covered effectively and counter-punched at the cut eye."
----------------------------------------------------------
From Frank Litsky in the August 6th edition of The New York Times:

Undaunted by Riot, Garden to Continue Boxing; Damage Is Minimal -- Next Card Set For Aug. 24 Fight Director Says the Spectators Just Went Haywire

Boxing, Harry Markson said yesterday, will continue at Madison Square Garden. But he hopes that future customers] will refrain from "excessive exuberance.'"

 Markson is director of boxing at the Garden. He was one of 7,000 who watched Wednesday night's bruising double-header at America's most famous sports arena. 

The first half was a 10-round fight between Gabriel (Flash) Elorde of the Philippines and Frankie Narvaez of Puerto Rico and New York. Elorde won an unpopular split decision, and that led to the second and unscheduled-part of the program, a 20-minute riot. 

"The damage was minimal," Markson said. "All those chair sections were pushed over, and the pictures of them made the place look like a battlefield. But I'll tell you this. In the 40 years the Garden has been here, there has never been anything like this." 

About 100 persons seemed to be involved in smashing chairs, light bulbs, telephone booths and much more. Fire axes, fire extinguishers and broken whisky bottles flew threw the Garden. Someone estimated the damage at $10,000, all covered by insurance. 

At least eight men were injured inside and outside the Garden. They included two of the five men arrested. The five were held in lieu of bail yesterday for Criminal Court hearings next week. One was charged with felonious assault and four with malicious mischief. Jesus Valez, 34 years old, of 414 West 25th Street faces a hearing Wednesday on a charge of throwing a brick in a fireman's face. Judge Abraham M. Roth set bail at $2,500.

Judge Robert U. Molloy set $500 bail for the four others, who will have hearings on Thursday. They are José Belaquex, 22, 973 Willoughby Street, Brooklyn; Bartolo Torres, 23, 335 West 21st Street; Raul Batista, 22, of 69 Norfolk Street, and Louis Muniz 24 132 East 112th Street.

"We had 70 of our special policemen on duty," said Markson. "That was 20 more than usual. But if we had 150 policemen, it wouldn't have been different. People just went haywire."

"The Puerto Rican people are fair," said José Figueroa of 240 Madison Street, who said he was a cousin of Narvaez. "We cheer for the winner, but only when he is the real winner. This was, what you say, a miscarriage of justice. Then we get angry.” 

Until this riot, most of the Garden unruliness had come at wrestling shows. 

The next sports events at the Garden are wrestling on Aug. 23 and boxing the next night. 

The boxing program will have three 10-round bouts, topped by a light-heavyweight; contest between Jimmy Dupree of New York and Johnny Persol of Brooklyn. 

In October, the Garden hopes to have Joey Giardello defend the middleweight championship against Dick Tiger. And on the same card, Markson said, he would like to have an Elorde-Narvaez rematch. "They staged a magnificent fight," Markson said, “and both sides seem interested in a rematch. But Narvaez has a cut over his right eye and doesn't want to fight until October." Narvaez is managed by Sandy Schwartz and Jack Riley. Schwartz said after the fight that Narvaez would never fight in New York again, not because of the decision (though he disagreed with it), but because Narvaez got only $3,700 as his 20 per cent share of the net gate. Elorde had a $10,000 guarantee. However, Markson said Riley "was not adverse" to a rematch. John Condon, the Garden's director of boxing publicity, was perturbed by the Page 1 headline of an afternoon newspaper saying: "BOXING FLOORED AGAIN." "That's not fair," said Condon. "The fight was magnificent. Boxing had a great night. People, not boxing, ruined it."

"You're right," said Markson. "You don't abandon a sport for one thing like this.”

PALPAK NA FLOOD CONTROL PROJECT SA TONDO

Hindi tinanggap ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) ang pag-take over sa P774-million flood control project na Sunog Apog pumping station sa Tondo, Manila dahil umano sa mga sira nito.

Sa panayam sa “Ted Failon at DJ Chacha” ng True FM, sinabi ni Manila 2nd District Rep. Rolando Valeriano na September 2022 pa sinubukang ilipat ng Department of Public Works and Highway (DPWH) ang proyekto sa MMDA.
